content: {"summary":"Card payments failed from midnight 2025‑01‑14 because the client certificate presented by the card‑processor‑proxy pods expired at that moment. The expiration triggered CPX‑E600 handshake errors on both proxy pods, causing every outbound call to the processor to fail. A new certificate was obtained via a CSR submitted to the processor, the Kubernetes Secret `card-processor-client-tls` was updated with the new cert, and the proxy deployment was restarted, after which the errors stopped.","likely_cause":"Expired processor‑issued client certificate used by card‑processor‑proxy","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The client certificate presented by the proxy expired at 00:00 on 2025‑01‑14.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#2","INC-0004#0"],"quote":"notAfter=Jan 14 00:00:00 2025 GMT"},{"text":"Expiration caused CPX‑E600 handshake failures on both proxy pods, leading to payment failures.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#0","RB-023#1"],"quote":"CPX-E600 handshake failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate"},{"text":"The replacement was done by generating a CSR, uploading it to the processor, receiving a new cert, updating the `card-processor-client-tls` Secret, and restarting the deployment.","evidence_ids":["RB-023#3","INC-0004#0"],"quote":"replace the Secret, then restart: the proxy only reads it at start"}],"next_checks":["Verify the current `card-processor-client-tls` Secret contains a certificate with a future `notAfter` date","Confirm the proxy pods have restarted and are no longer logging CPX‑E600","Monitor payments‑api for PAYAPI‑E1107 errors to ensure they remain at baseline","Set up alerts for certificate expiry 30 days and 7 days before `notAfter`"]}
